content: The parties sought division of a flat, garage, and parking; the property was assigned as marital home to Partner 2 with a child. The interpretive problem: whether the right of habitation reduces market value in equalization. Framed under art. 720 c.c. and case law, the court found the property not conveniently divisible and assigned it to Partner 2 with a cash equalization of half the market value. Principles: assignment of the family home is a personal right that extinguishes when ownership consolidates; valuation remains full market price without reduction; equalization reflects 50%. Costs, including expert fees, were compensated. 1.
